_comment: May this app write to YOU, its operator, about its own operation — a queue waiting for an answer, something that stopped working? Read it only through isOperatorNotifyEnabled() (lib/notify/config.ts), never by re-reading this file. Unlike almost every other switch here it ships ON, and that is deliberate: every job that sends through this channel carries its own 'enabledByDefault': false, and two off states in series make a channel nobody ever finds — the first of them only findable by reading a config file you did not know existed. The recipient is the owner of the app, not a customer, so the unwanted-contact risk the community's and the setup surface's switches fall towards does not exist here. ⚠️ A BROKEN file is still off: an unknown key, a wrong type or a language this app does not have drops the WHOLE file back to the code default, which is 'enabled': false. Both directions are on purpose — 'what does a fresh product do' and 'what does an unreadable file mean' are two questions, and the honest answers differ. Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored. Nothing sends through this channel in a fresh app; switching it off is a deploy, like every switch here.
_comment_locale: Which language operator mail is written in — one of the codes in i18n/config.ts (LOCALES). It lives HERE because it lives nowhere else: the users table has no language column, and the app's only other language source is a cookie, which is precisely what a scheduled job does not have. An unknown code is a broken file by the rule above, not a fallback.
